_note: Real-world inputs for the drive sim. Every number is an [estimate] (typical range from general knowledge, from docs/realism lesson plan) until someone checks it against a named source (Gillespie, Milliken, Bentley/Haynes) and re-tags it verified. SI units: kg, m, N. Tire pressure in psi.

bug._source: [estimate] stock air-cooled Bug-class curb mass 750-850 kg, CG ~0.5 m, ~40/60 front/rear split. baseFrontFraction is how far from the rear axle toward the front axle the CG sits (0.42 = 42% of wheelbase)

surfaces._source: [estimate] grip = peak friction coefficient, rrCoef = rolling resistance coefficient (force = rrCoef x load). Ranges from the realism lesson plan. 'pavement' and 'gravel' are listed for the planned roads and trails; the current world draws dirt, sand, rock and mud.

tire._source: [estimate] street 28-32 psi, sand/rock driving 12-20 psi. Lower pressure widens the contact patch: floats on soft ground (less rolling resistance, more grip), but costs steering response on hard ground and risks pinch flats on rock.

engine._source: [estimate] Air-cooled flat-four character: modest torque, flat mid-range. torqueCurve is normalised (1 = peak) as [rpm, fraction]. Gear ratios are Baja-style (trade top speed for pull); final drive is solved so top gear reaches the vehicle top speed at redline on the reference tire. Heat: air-cooled, so cooling depends on airflow (road speed) plus the fan. Thresholds in deg C.

diff._source: [estimate] open: torque limited by the weaker wheel; lsd: strong wheel can take up to biasRatio x the weak wheel plus a preload; locker: both wheels driven, each limited only by its own grip.
